task_summary: Parse a BibTeX file, verify each citation against academic APIs (CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, DBLP), identify fake/hallucinated citations, and output results as JSON.
decomposition_rationale: The task naturally splits into three concerns: (1) parsing and cleaning BibTeX data, (2) verifying citations against external APIs with robust querying, and (3) scoring matches and producing the final output. This separation keeps I/O, network logic, and decision logic independent.

skills.name: evo-bibtex-parser
skills.description: Parses BibTeX files using bibtexparser 1.4.2 and cleans LaTeX/BibTeX artifacts from fields like title, author, year, DOI, and venue. Produces a normalized list of citation dictionaries ready for verification.
skills.responsibility: BibTeX file loading, field extraction, LaTeX artifact removal, and normalization of citation metadata
dr_sections: 6. Navigating Edge Cases, Pitfalls, and Data Anomalies

skills.name: evo-citation-verifier
skills.description: Queries external academic APIs (CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, DBLP, doi.org) to verify whether a citation exists. Implements robust HTTP sessions with retry logic, exponential backoff, and rate limiting for unauthenticated access.
skills.responsibility: Network communication with academic APIs, DOI resolution, rate limiting, retry logic, and returning raw API results for each citation
dr_sections: 3. Landscape of Free Academic Citation Verification APIs
5. Practical Implementation of Robust API Querying

skills.name: evo-citation-scorer
skills.description: Compares parsed BibTeX citation metadata against API results using fuzzy string matching and multi-factor scoring to classify citations as real or fake, then outputs the final JSON report.
skills.responsibility: String normalization, fuzzy title/author matching, composite confidence scoring, fake/real classification, and JSON output generation
dr_sections: 1. Introduction to the Phenomenon of Hallucinated Citations
